message.reasoning: The question asks why lithium and sodium behave alike. Option C is straightforwardly false: lithium is in period 2, sodium in period 3. Option A restates the shared behaviour rather than explaining it, since both forming 1+ ions is the thing to be explained. Option D is an irrelevant correlate; beryllium is also light and behaves quite differently. That leaves B. Both elements sit in Group 1, so both have a single electron in their outermost shell. Losing that one electron gives a stable noble-gas configuration, which is why each forms a 1+ cation and bonds ionically with chloride.
